reviews.title: Profanity Necessary? Really?
reviews.text:
The strong profanity would cause me to never suggest this app to preteens. Memrise confirmed to me that it’s intentional. There should be a setting for parents to disable that.

The app might be helpful only if used to supplement other language-learning apps or methods. By itself, it’s insufficient.

Many video clips have terrible audio quality because the speaker isn’t using a dedicated microphone. Very unprofessional.

reviews.title: A stunningly awful, AI-slop language app in a sea of awful, AI-slop language apps
reviews.text:
I tried Memrise years ago, before the app, and liked it, so a positive experience with the free version of the app was enough for me to pay what I thought was a reasonable price for all-access.
Within 6 months, all actual learning content had been swapped out for broken versions: vocabulary lessons with some words having a blank instead of a translation, or some vocab “words” that were not words, but were compound sentences using tenses and phrases I was never taught. There were—and still are—multiple choice questions that have the same answer for 3 of 4 options, which means even if you know the answer, you’ll probably be wrong. The video section that once had original content from native speakers is now flooded with stolen videos from creators on YouTube who offer their videos for free—but Memrise is using in its paid service, without credit and probably without compensation for the creator, who originally offered it FOR FREE. And as if all that wasn’t bad enough—and it most assuredly is—Memrise added the dreaded AI “helper”bots, just like every other corner-cutting language app out there. Naturally, the bots were messy and never worked right, but I was told to just wait it out because they were still in beta. The myriad of other, bot-unrelated issues I pointed out were, of course, ignored. And then something happened that would be so much funnier if I hadn’t paid Memrise for an all-access lifetime sub. The app also lost its user flexibility it once had: people’s learning lists made way for “you must learn these words, in these lessons” and it’s too controlled, locked down, and not fun. Ditch the AI.

reviews.title: Memrise is broken & No way to Report It!
reviews.text:
The current state of Memrise does not save any of your progress. You complete a lesson in the Scenarios section, and when you return to the page, it is like it never happened.  
As a workaround I manually update my streak to keep the count going.
If you log out and back in, your streak is back to zero and all progress is lost. You are set back in time to an earlier level.
Something broke along the way but nothing has been fixed!
And, there  is no way to report this issue! The help section has documentation without any way of contacting support directly.
Since I cannot save progress for one to two weeks now and nobody has fixed it, this has become a one star app!

Fix your broken app already!

reviews.title: I wish they’d roll back to an earlier version
reviews.text:
I would originally given this app an infinite number of stars out of 10 but unfortunately the new update has taken away the most valued features I found in the app. 

Before you would learn a set structure of lessons in a set order and you could revisit them easily and as often as you liked. A lot of my current language level came from the consistency of repeating manageable sized lessons over and over again at my own pace 

The new version of the app has taken away the set structure and introduced ‘word lists’. Some of these lists are hundreds of words long with all the categories mixed together and you are limited to a once daily review of words instead of being able to freely go back and practice bite sized modules. 

The lists that are ‘community made’ and some of the memrise made ones also lack the native speaker videos and pronunciation dialogue that originally played when learning new words which is a massive hindrance when learning a language like Japanese that relies on the inflection used when speaking. 

I now feel extremely sad that I originally signed up for a whole year subscription because of how great it was and 6 months in I find much less value in the app to the point that I hardly open it anymore. 

Please bring the good features back Memrise

reviews.title: Weird logistical failures
reviews.text:
There are no level tests or objective (C.E.F.R.) levels to choose from — you have to select your own from vague descriptions. Choosing the highest level still only places you early in the course, so in some languages the lessons are far below my level and I can’t accelerate up. Worse still, the only way to change between the available levels is to delete all your progress and start again — this is absolutely ludicrous. 

If you delay for just a few moments, because you’re doing something in real life, it closes the lesson and you have to start again. I use a lot of language apps and this is the only one like that — others only do it after a significant amount of time, if at all. 

It’s annoying that the streak is per language, as doing all the ones I’m studying every day is a burden. On the other hand, you can manually change your streak to anything , which is ridiculous.

reviews.title: Japanese is ridiculous
reviews.text:
It gets complicated far too quickly and doesn't explain how sentences are constructed or grammar works, so you can't use the sentences to model your own. 

The app goes from simple words to complicated sentences that are spoken far too fast to make out this individual words. They're also not particularly useful because they're so specific - I'm currently being hit with 'I'm a shy person at first. I talk to people when I get to know them', and the app hasn't even covered basics like numbers and directions!

The AI chat bot are an interesting idea, but presume a level of fluency way above what you actually have. They're poorly implemented and should surely be tailored to the level you are working at.

All in all, a frustrating experience and not one I'd pay premium for.
